fieldMarks: Pig-like; grizzled black and gray with a dark stripe down the back.
Whitish collar across the shoulders in adults.
Young are reddish to yellowish brown with a black back stripe.
Musk (scent) gland on the rump; adults about 35–55 lb.
behavior: Lives in herds of a few to several dozen animals.
Mainly active early morning and late afternoon, somewhat nocturnal; huddles on cool nights.
Eats prickly pear and other succulents, roots, fruits, nuts and mesquite beans; leaves shredded cactus pads and uprooted plants.
Communicates with grunts, growls and tooth 'pops'; very poor eyesight but a keen sense of smell.
habitat: Brushy semidesert where prickly pear is conspicuous; dense thickets, rocky canyons, chaparral and scrub oak. In Arizona from desert floor to about 7,000 ft, usually below 5,500 ft.
range: Arizona, New Mexico and western and southern Texas, south through Mexico to Argentina; not in Canada. Introduced populations exist in north-central Texas.

lookalikes.name: Feral hog
lookalikes.howToTell: Peccaries are native New World animals, whereas pigs are Old World species introduced from Europe; the peccary shows a whitish shoulder collar.
